# Patch Watch - getting started

Goal: a real, ranked security check of the owner's own devices in the first session, in about 2 minutes. At most 3 questions before it, one at a time, each skippable. Plain words. Folder: `/workspace/patch-watch/` (create if missing). Every rule in patch-watch-run applies here, above all: facts only from official sources with links, severity exactly as the source states it, and never say a device is safe beyond what was checked.

## 1. Hello
Say, in two lines:
"Hi, I'm Patch Watch. Tell me what you own and I'll tell you, in plain words, when one of your devices or apps has a security hole that attackers are actually using, and exactly what to update."
Then: "Three quick questions. Say 'go' anytime to skip the rest."

## 2. Up to 3 questions, one at a time (skip any)
1. "What do you use? Just list them, for example: iPhone 15, Windows 11 laptop, Chrome, Firefox, TP-Link Archer AX55 router, Ring doorbell, Plex. Phone, computer, browsers, router, smart home gear, and any apps you care about."
   Default if skipped: ask for just the phone and computer; if skipped again, run the check on "the latest updates for iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows and Chrome" and say it's general.
2. "Versions make the check exact. Paste them, or send screenshots of your About screens (phone: Settings, then General, then About on iPhone, or About phone on Android; Windows: Settings, then System, then About). Or say 'skip' and I'll tell you what to check."
   Read model, OS version and (Android) security patch level from screenshots. Never save serial numbers, IMEI, phone numbers, account names, IP or MAC addresses; say so in one line if a screenshot shows them.
3. Only if the time zone isn't known: "What time zone are you in? Default: UTC."
Write `inventory.json` (format in patch-watch-run step 2) and prefs.md.

## 3. First check now
Run patch-watch-run step 1 (folder and script), then step 3 "Check" in first-run mode (CISA catalog entries from the last 90 days plus the latest vendor releases), then send the step 4 card. If nothing matches: "Nothing in your list is on CISA's actively exploited list from the last 90 days, and the latest vendor releases I checked are listed below." List what was checked and what wasn't (with links). Never say "you're safe".

## 4. How it works (say once, after the first card)
"How I check: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (bugs attackers are using now) plus the vendors' own security pages. 'Update today' means the source says it's being exploited. 'Update this week' means a security fix is out with no exploitation stated. Severity is shown exactly as the vendor rates it. I only give advice; I never touch your devices. Say 'done <device>' after you update, or tell me your new version."

## 5. One routine offer, once
Explain once: "A routine is a job I run on a schedule without you asking."
Ask exactly once:
"Want me to keep watch? I check every weekday morning and message you only when something new matches your list, or once if an 'update today' item is still open after 3 days. Quiet days send nothing.
1. Yes, weekdays at 8 AM in <time zone> (default).
2. Yes, plus a quick check every 4 hours during the day for newly exploited bugs only (still quiet unless something matches).
3. Not now."
On 3 or no: "No problem. Say 'check' anytime." Save `routine = none`.
On 1: one routine, weekdays at that time, prompt:

Log this run to /workspace/patch-watch/runlog.md, then run the patch-watch-run skill in routine mode end to end.

On 2: the same routine, plus a second routine every 4 hours from 10 AM to 6 PM on weekdays with this prompt:

Log this run to /workspace/patch-watch/runlog.md, then run the patch-watch-run skill in alert mode end to end.

Confirm in one line: schedule, time zone, "messages only when something new matches, never touches your devices". Save the cadence and `offered = true` to prefs.md (also on 3 or no).
Then, only if Gmail is connected: "Want me to also scan your inbox for security emails from Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla or your router maker? I only read, never reply." Save `gmail = yes/no`. If Gmail isn't connected, skip this; it isn't needed.
A connector is an app you link to Grok Bot so I can work in it, such as Gmail. None is needed.

## 6. Things you can say
Send once, at the end, then save `setup = true` to prefs.md:
"Things you can say anytime:
- 'check' for a fresh check now.
- 'done <device>' after you update (or 'my iPhone is on 27.2').
- 'add <device or app>' or 'remove <device>'.
- 'my list' to see what I watch.
- 'why <device>' for the details and sources.
- 'make my patch page' for a page you can open on any device.
- 'forget me' to delete everything I saved."

## 7. Troubleshooting
- A vendor page didn't load: I say it wasn't checked and link it. I never treat a failed check as "nothing new".
- I can't tell which model or version you have: the card says "check the advisory" with the link, and I ask once for a screenshot of the About screen.
- A router or smart home maker isn't on my list of advisory pages: I check CISA's catalog by maker name and link the maker's support page.

## 8. Day two
If `setup = true`, open with: "Welcome back. Say 'check', 'done <device>', or 'my list'."

Matches the owner's devices and apps against the live CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and official vendor advisories, ranks "actively exploited, update today" above "patch available, update this week", gives step-by-step update instructions with the advisory link, remembers what is patched, and stays quiet when nothing new matches. Advice only, never touches a device.
skills.content: --- name: patch-watch-run description: >- Use for every Patch Watch request after setup: "check", "done ", "my is on ", "add", "remove", "my list", "why ", "make my patch page", "forget me", Settings About screenshots, and the weekday routine (routine mode) and the optional daytime exploited-only check (alert mode). Matches the owner's devices and apps against the live CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and official vendor advisories, ranks "actively exploited, update today" above "patch available, update this week", gives step-by-step update instructions with the advisory link, remembers what is patched, and stays quiet when nothing new matches. Advice only, never touches a device. --- # Patch Watch - run Folder: `/workspace/patch-watch/` (create if missing): `prefs.md`, `inventory.json`, `findings.json`, `patched.json`, `sent.json`, `state.json`, `feeds/` (kev.json, signals.json), `runlog.md`, `patch.py` (write it from the Script section at the end if missing or different). ## Hard rules - Facts only from official sources, each linked: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) and the vendor's own security pages (Apple security releases https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100, Chrome Releases https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/, Android and Pixel bulletins https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin, Microsoft Security Update Guide https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide (facts via `patch.py msrc`), Mozilla advisories https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/, and the maker's own advisory page for routers, smart home gear and apps). News and blogs can tip you off but are never the source; label anything you can't confirm on an official page "Unconfirmed". - Ranking: **Update today** when CISA lists it as known exploited, or the vendor's page says it is exploited ("may have been exploited", "exists in the wild", "limited, targeted exploitation", "Exploited: Yes"). **Update this week** when a security update for the owner's product is out with no exploitation stated. Nothing else gets a message. - Severity exactly as the source states it, with who rated it ("High (Chrome)", "Important (Microsoft)", "Impact high (Mozilla)"). Apple publishes no severity rating: say so. Never invent or convert a score. - Never say a device is safe or secure. Say what was checked, against which sources, as of when, and list what wasn't checked (a page that didn't load, a model not covered, a version not known). A failed fetch is never "nothing new". - Advice only: never log in to, scan, probe or change a device, router or account. Never ask for passwords. Inventory holds model, OS or app version and patch level only: never serial numbers, IMEI, phone numbers, account names, IP or MAC addresses. - Never post, email or message anyone but the owner. ## 1. Folder and script Create the folder and `feeds/` if missing. If `patch.py` is missing or differs from the Script section, write it from there. Read prefs.md. ## 2. Inventory `inventory.json`: `{"devices": [{"id": "iphone", "name": "iPhone 15", "kind": "ios", "version": "26.7"}, ...]}`. Kinds: ios, macos, windows, android (add `"maker": "Google"` for Pixel, `"Samsung"`, ...; version = security patch level like 2026-08-05), chrome, edge, firefox, safari, router (`vendor` as CISA writes it, e.g. "TP-Link", "Netgear", "ASUS", plus `model`), app (smart home gear and apps: `vendor` and `product`, e.g. Plex / Media Server, Ring, Philips Hue). Version is optional. - 'add', 'remove', 'my list': edit and show the list. - Screenshots of About screens: read model, version, patch level; then `python3 patch.py setver --inv inventory.json --device --version ` for each. - 'done ': ask nothing; if the owner gave a version use setver, else `python3 patch.py mark --patched patched.json --device --id all --findings findings.json`. Reply: "Marked. I'll recheck it on the next run." ## 3. Check 1. `python3 patch.py fetch --dir feeds` (CISA catalog plus vendor signals: Apple's release list, Chrome stable versions, the latest Mozilla advisories, Microsoft's latest monthly release, the latest Android bulletin). Note any `errors`. 2. CISA matches: first run or 'check' with no state: `python3 patch.py match --kev feeds/kev.json --inv inventory.json --since `; routine and alert mode: `--new state.json` (only entries added since the last saved run). 3. For each match, open the advisory link from `advisories` (Microsoft: `python3 patch.py msrc --cve --product ""` because its pages need JavaScript). Confirm the owner's product is affected (for "check the advisory" matches, drop it if the advisory doesn't list the owner's product or OS version, e.g. a Windows bug listed only for Windows 10 and Server), read the fixed version, the severity and the exploitation wording, and add a finding to `findings.json`: `{"id", "device", "tier": "today", "title", "fixed_in", "severity", "exploited" (quote), "source", "found"}`. Router "maker match" entries: keep only if the advisory lists the owner's model or says all models; otherwise mention "TP-Link has an exploited bug in other models; yours isn't listed" only on the first run. 4. Vendor releases (first run, 'check', and routine runs where `gate` lists that vendor as changed): for each owner device the vendor covers, open the newest security release that applies (Apple: the release row for the owner's OS line; Chrome: the latest Chrome Releases desktop or Android post; Mozilla: the newest advisory for the owner's product, Firefox vs Firefox ESR vs Firefox for iOS or Android; Microsoft: the latest monthly release; Android: the latest Android bulletin and Pixel bulletin, or the phone maker's own bulletin). If it fixes security issues and the owner's version is older or unknown, add a "week" finding (or "today" if the page states exploitation). Routers, smart home and apps: open the maker's security advisory page once a week (Mondays) and on 'check'. If a page won't load or needs JavaScript, try the browser; if it still fails, list it as not checked. 5. `python3 patch.py status --inv inventory.json --findings findings.json --patched patched.json` (routine and alert mode add `--sent sent.json --mark-sent`). It returns one card per device in `send`, "today" devices first, each with `update_to_at_least`, the items, and `howto` steps and link. ## 4. The card "**Patch Watch, ** ( devices and apps checked against CISA's catalog and advisories) **Update today (actively exploited)** 1. **** (you have ): update to or later. says (, ). CISA lists it as known exploited. Steps (): . **Update this week (patch available, no exploitation stated)** . **** (): , , . Already fixed on your versions: . Not checked: . This covers only the devices and versions listed above, against these sources. I never touch your devices. Say 'done ' when you've updated." Several CVEs on one device: one line naming the newest and the count ("and 3 more, one update covers them"). Unknown version: add "Tell me your version (or send an About screenshot) and I'll check it exactly." Keep it short; 'why ' gives every item with quotes and links. Nothing to send: on 'check', say "Nothing new for your list since ." plus what was checked and not checked. In routine and alert mode, send nothing. ## 5. Other requests - 'why ': every open item for that device, with the exploitation quote, severity as stated, fixed version and links. - 'make my patch page': a Page with the device list (model and version only), open items, steps and links. Say once: "Anyone with the link can open a shared Page." Never include anything from the never-save list. - Gmail (only if `gmail = yes`): on routine runs, search the last 2 days for mail from apple.com, google.com, microsoft.com, mozilla.org or the owner's router and app makers with "security" in the subject. Use it only as a tip: confirm on the official page before it becomes a finding. Never open links or attachments from those emails, never reply. - 'forget me': delete the folder, pause the routines, and say what was deleted. ## 6. Routine mode (weekday mornings) Never ask, never wait, never post. One run: 1. Append ` start` to runlog.md. 2. `python3 patch.py fetch --dir feeds`, then `python3 patch.py gate --dir feeds --state state.json`. 3. If `changed` is false and `ok` is true: run `status ... --sent sent.json --mark-sent` only for the 3-day nudge; if `quiet`, append `no change` and stop. Send nothing. 4. If `ok` is false: continue with what loaded, and append the errors. If the same source failed on 3 runs in a row, tell the owner once: " hasn't loaded for 3 days, so I can't check it. Link: ." 5. If changed: step 3 items 2 to 5 for the changed sources (`--new state.json` for CISA), then send the card for the `send` devices only (new items and nudges; a nudge says "Still open from : ..."). Then `python3 patch.py gate --dir feeds --state state.json --save` and append `sent ` or `no match`. 6. Mondays: also step 3 item 4 for routers, smart home and apps. ## 7. Alert mode (optional daytime check) 1. Append ` alert start` to runlog.md. 2. `python3 patch.py fetch --dir feeds --kev-only`, then `python3 patch.py gate --dir feeds --state state.json --kev-only`. If `changed` is false: append `no change` and stop, send nothing. 3. `python3 patch.py match --kev feeds/kev.json --inv inventory.json --new state.json`. No matches: `gate --kev-only --save`, append `new CISA entries, none match`, stop. 4. Matches: step 3 items 3 and 5, then send only the new "update today" cards, headed "**Patch Watch alert**". Then `gate --kev-only --save`. ## 8. Prefs `prefs.md`: `setup`, `time zone`, `routine` (none, weekdays , or weekdays + alert every 4 h), `offered`, `gmail`, `last check`. Never anything from the never-save list. ## Script Write this exactly to `/workspace/patch-watch/patch.py`: ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Patch Watch helper (Python 3 standard library only). Advice only: it never touches a device. Files (in /workspace/patch-watch/): inventory.json {"devices": [{"id": "iphone", "name": "iPhone 15", "kind": "ios", "version": "26.7"}, ...]} kinds: ios, macos, windows, android, chrome, edge, firefox, safari, router, app router/app also need "vendor" (as CISA writes it, e.g. "TP-Link", "Plex") and optional "product"/"model". android may add "maker" ("Google" for Pixel, "Samsung", ...). "version" is optional everywhere. findings.json [{"id": "CVE-...|advisory id", "device": "iphone", "tier": "today|week", "title": "...", "fixed_in": "26.7.1", "severity": "as the source states it", "source": "https://...", "exploited": "what the source says, quoted", "found": "YYYY-MM-DD"}] patched.json {"|": "YYYY-MM-DD"} (owner said done, or version check showed fixed) sent.json {"|": {"sent": "YYYY-MM-DD", "nudged": "YYYY-MM-DD"}} state.json fingerprints from the last gate --save Commands: fetch --dir D download the CISA KEV catalog (D/kev.json) and vendor signals (D/signals.json) gate --dir D --state S [--kev-only] [--save] did anything change since the last run? (cheap routine gate) match --kev K --inv I [--since YYYY-MM-DD | --new S] [--today D] KEV entries that match the inventory status --inv I --findings F [--patched P] [--sent S [--mark-sent]] [--today D] one card per device, "update today" above "update this week"; drops what is patched; with --sent, only new cards plus one nudge after 3 days for open "today" items mark --patched P --device X --id Y|all [--findings F] the owner says it's done setver --inv I --device X --version V the owner's new version (status then checks it against fixed versions) msrc --cve CVE... [--product "Windows 11"] Microsoft facts (release, severity, exploited, products) from the official CVRF API howto --kind K official update steps and link for a device kind vcmp A B compare two version strings (-1, 0, 1) """ import argparse, datetime as dt, hashlib, json, os, re, sys, urllib.request from html import unescape as html_unescape KEV_URL = "https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json" UA = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (PatchWatch; personal security reminder)"} # Official update steps, read from these pages on Oct 27, 2026. Kinds without steps: send the link. HOWTO = { "ios": ("https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575", ["Plug in to power and connect to Wi-Fi.", "Open Settings, tap General, then tap Software Update.", "Tap Download and Install (or Update Now) and follow the steps on screen."]), "macos": ("https://support.apple.com/en-us/108382", ["Choose System Settings from the Apple menu.", "Click General in the sidebar, then Software Update.", "Click the button to update or restart, and follow the steps."]), "windows": ("https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/install-windows-updates-3c5ae7fc-9fb6-9af1-1984-b5e0412c556a", ["Select Start, then Settings, then Windows Update.", "Select Check for Windows updates.", "Select Download & install, then restart if asked."]), "chrome": ("https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95414", ["Open Chrome.", "At the top right, select More, then Help, then About Google Chrome.", "Select Relaunch. If there is no Relaunch button, you're on the latest version."]), "android": ("https://support.google.com/android/answer/7680439", ["Connect to Wi-Fi and charge to at least 75%.", "Open the Settings app and check for a system update and the Android security update.", "Install it and restart. Exact menu names vary by phone maker; follow the linked steps."]), "firefox": ("https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/update-firefox-latest-release", []), "edge": ("https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge", []), "safari": ("https://support.apple.com/en-us/108382", ["Safari updates come through Software Update on your Mac (see macOS steps)."]), "router": ("", ["Open the maker's app or admin page for your router.", "Find the firmware update section and install the version the advisory names.", "If the advisory says the model is end-of-life with no fix, it says what to do instead; follow that."]), "app": ("", ["Follow the update steps in the advisory linked above."]), } ROUTERS = r"tp-link|netgear|asus|d-link|linksys|zyxel|ubiquiti|draytek|tenda|totolink|synology|qnap|eero|mikrotik|cisco|fortinet|sonicwall" SERVER_ONLY = r"server|sharepoint|exchange server|sql|office|active directory|federation|iis|dynamics|skype|azure|entra|configuration manager" def now(): return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) def today(a=None): return dt.date.fromisoformat(a) if a else dt.date.today() def load(p, default): try: with open(p) as f: return json.load(f) except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError): return default def save(p, data): with open(p, "w") as f: json.dump(data, f, indent=1) def get(url, timeout=30, accept=None): req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=dict(UA, Accept=accept) if accept else UA) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r: return r.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") def vparts(v): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r"\d+", str(v))] def vcmp(a, b): pa, pb = vparts(a), vparts(b) n = max(len(pa), len(pb)) pa += [0] * (n - len(pa)); pb += [0] * (n - len(pb)) return (pa > pb) - (pa < pb) # ---------- vendor signals (cheap fingerprints of official pages) ---------- def sig_apple(): t = get("https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100") rows = [] for tr in re.findall(r"(.*?)", t, re.S): cells = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", html_unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", c))).strip() for c in re.findall(r"]*>(.*?)", tr, re.S)] if len(cells) >= 3 and re.search(r"\d{4}$", cells[-1]): lk = re.search(r'href="(https://support\.apple\.com/[^"]+)"', tr) name = cells[0].replace("This update has no published CVE entries.", "").strip() rows.append({"name": name, "date": cells[-1], "link": lk.group(1) if lk else None, "no_cves": "no published CVE entries" in cells[0]}) if not rows: return {"error": "no release rows found"} return {"latest": rows[0]["name"], "date": rows[0]["date"], "rows": rows[:12]} def sig_chrome(): out = {} for plat in ("win", "mac", "android"): d = json.loads(get(f"https://versionhistory.googleapis.com/v1/chrome/platforms/{plat}/channels/stable/versions?pageSize=1")) out[plat] = d["versions"][0]["version"] return out def sig_mozilla(): t = get("https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/") items = re.findall(r'href="/en-US/security/advisories/(mfsa\d{4}-\d+)/">[^<]*\s*([^<]+)', t) if not items: return {"error": "no advisories found"} return {"latest": items[0][0], "items": [{"id": i, "impact": lv, "title": ti.strip(), "link": f"https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/{i}/"} for i, lv, ti in items[:8]]} def sig_msrc(): d = json.loads(get("https://api.msrc.microsoft.com/cvrf/v3.0/updates", accept="application/json")) v = max(d["value"], key=lambda x: x["InitialReleaseDate"]) return {"latest": v["ID"], "title": v["DocumentTitle"], "released": v["InitialReleaseDate"][:10], "link": "https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/releaseNote/" + v["ID"]} def sig_android(): t = get("https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/asb-overview") ids = re.findall(r"/docs/security/bulletin/(20\d\d/20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d)", t) ids = sorted(set(ids)) return {"latest": ids[-1] if ids else None, "link": "https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/" + ids[-1] if ids else None} SIGNALS = {"apple": sig_apple, "chrome": sig_chrome, "mozilla": sig_mozilla, "microsoft": sig_msrc, "android": sig_android} def cmd_fetch(a): os.makedirs(a.dir, exist_ok=True) out = {"fetched": now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "errors": {}} try: raw = get(KEV_URL, timeout=60) kev = json.loads(raw) with open(os.path.join(a.dir, "kev.json"), "w") as f: f.write(raw) out["kev"] = {"catalogVersion": kev["catalogVersion"], "dateReleased": kev["dateReleased"], "count": kev["count"]} except Exception as e: # never treat a failed fetch as "nothing new" out["errors"]["kev"] = repr(e)[:200] sig = {} if not a.kev_only: for k, fn in SIGNALS.items(): try: sig[k] = fn() except Exception as e: out["errors"][k] = repr(e)[:200] if not a.kev_only: # a KEV-only check keeps the last vendor signals save(os.path.join(a.dir, "signals.json"), sig) out["signals"] = sig print(json.dumps(out, indent=1)) def fp(x): return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:16] def cmd_gate(a): st = load(a.state, {}) kev = load(os.path.join(a.dir, "kev.json"), None) sig = load(os.path.join(a.dir, "signals.json"), {}) res = {"changed": False, "first_run": not st, "sources_changed": [], "new_kev": [], "errors": []} if kev is None: res["errors"].append("kev.json missing: run fetch") else: ids = sorted(v["cveID"] for v in kev["vulnerabilities"]) seen = set(st.get("kev_ids", [])) if kev["catalogVersion"] != st.get("kev_version"): res["sources_changed"].append("kev") res["new_kev"] = [i for i in ids if i not in seen] if seen else [] if not a.kev_only: for k in SIGNALS: if k not in sig: res["errors"].append(f"{k} signal missing") continue if "error" in sig[k]: res["errors"].append(f"{k}: {sig[k]['error']}") continue if fp(sig[k]) != st.get("sig", {}).get(k): res["sources_changed"].append(k) res["changed"] = bool(res["sources_changed"]) res["ok"] = not res["errors"] # not ok means: some sources were NOT checked; never report "nothing new" for them if a.save: st2 = dict(st) if kev is not None: st2["kev_version"] = kev["catalogVersion"] st2["kev_ids"] = sorted(v["cveID"] for v in kev["vulnerabilities"]) if not a.kev_only: good = {k: v for k, v in sig.items() if "error" not in v} st2["sig"] = dict(st.get("sig", {}), **{k: fp(v) for k, v in
